root_cause.text: The USB framework unanchors URBs before invoking the completion callback, causing resubmitted URBs in kvaser_usb_read_bulk_callback() to become detached from the rx_submitted anchor and escape cleanup by usb_kill_anchored_urbs() during device removal.
root_cause.evidence: The patch explicitly re-anchors the URB to dev->rx_submitted immediately before resubmission (`usb_anchor_urb(urb, &dev->rx_submitted)`) and unanchors it only if resubmission fails (`usb_unanchor_urb(urb)`). The CVE description states: "the USB framework unanchors the URB before the complete function is called. This means that once an in-URB has been completed, it is no longer anchored and is ultimately not released in usb_kill_anchored_urbs()." This mismatch between the anchor lifecycle and URB resubmission in the completion callback is the root cause of the memory leak.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix URB lifecycle management by anchoring before submission and unanchoring on failure to prevent resource leaks and ensure proper tracking of in-flight USB requests.
intent_record.what: Added usb_anchor_urb() call before usb_submit_urb(), added early return on successful submission, and added usb_unanchor_urb() call in the error path before the existing error handling.
intent_record.how: The change anchors the URB to the device's rx_submitted anchor list before submission, allowing proper tracking and cleanup of in-flight requests. On successful submission, the function returns early, avoiding unnecessary error handling. On submission failure, the URB is unanchored before processing specific error codes, ensuring the anchor list remains consistent with actual submitted requests.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the error condition check from the else-if clause to ensure error messages are logged for all non-success paths in the USB read callback handler.
intent_record.what: Changed the conditional `else if (err)` to `else` on line 382, removing the explicit error check from the else-if clause.
intent_record.how: Previously, the error message would only print if `err` was non-zero. Now the error message prints unconditionally in the else branch, regardless of the `err` value. This means the error logging will execute even when `err` is 0 (success), which is logically incorrect and will print misleading error messages.
